title: Bob Barker allegations in explosive docuseries were 'true and then some,' former game show host says
summary: Former "Double Dare" host Marc Summers recalls Bob Barker's massive ego and cheap pay after Holly Hallstrom detailed her firing from "The Price Is Right" show.
story: Marc Summers, the former host of Nickelodeon's "Double Dare," appeared on "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia" to reflect on his experiences with the late "Price is Right" host, sharing stories about the TV icon's confidence and quirks.
Bob Barker may have been America's beloved game show host, but Marc Summers says there was another side to him behind the scenes.
The former host of Nickelodeon's hit game show "Double Dare" recently appeared on "Nostalgia Tonight with Joe Sibilia" to celebrate the show's 40th anniversary.

During the interview, Summers was asked about the recent E! docuseries "Dirty Rotten Scandals," which examines allegations that "The Price Is Right" was plagued by a hostile work environment, sexual harassment and discrimination.
OPRAH WINFREY ADMITS SHE BEGGED TALK SHOW AUDIENCE TO BURY FOOTAGE OF WHITNEY HOUSTON ONSTAGE FALL
Bob Barker, the beloved host of "The Price Is Right," passed away in 2023 at age 99. In March 2026, Barker was the subject of E!’s documentary series "Dirty Rotten Scandals." (Jesse Grant/WireImage)
Summers previously worked with Barker, who died in 2023 at 99.

"Well, I think it’s too bad that the man’s not around to defend himself," the 74-year-old told Sibilia. "However, everything on there was true and then some. I could tell you stories off the air that make your hair curl that were true."
Summers said Barker's ego didn't disappear when the cameras stopped rolling.
WATCH: MARC SUMMERS SAYS BOB BARKER'S EGO ‘WOULDN'T FIT IN THE ROOM’

"When Dorothy Jo (Barker's wife) passed away, he kind of became a different guy, and his ego wouldn't fit in the room," Summers said. "It was all about Bob. On his dressing room door and on his dress shirts, it said, 'WGMC' — 'World's Greatest MC.' Give me a break."
Bob Barker's wife, Dorothy Jo, died in 1981 at age 57. (Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)

Summers recalled that Studio 33, where "The Price Is Right" was taped, was occasionally used by other productions. During one such shoot, longtime "The Newlywed Game" host Bob Eubanks was filming a pilot when he hid the "WGMC" sign from Barker's dressing room door as a prank.

"So Barker comes in that Monday to do 'Price' and refuses to go on until they find the board that says 'WGMC,' and nobody could find it," Summers said. "They called up Eubanks at home and said, 'What the h--- did you do with this thing? We can't find it.' And Bob cracked up. He said, 'It's under the couch. Just lift up the couch. It is right under there.'"
Marc Summers hosted the original run of "Double Dare" for seven years. (Penske Media via Getty Images)
Looking back, Summers described himself as a 22-year-old "idea man" who got along with Barker. But the price wasn't always right when it came to working for him.
"He had a deal at CBS when they wanted to give him a raise on 'Price,' but they didn't have enough money to pay him more as a host," Summers said.

"So they made him an executive producer and gave him an overall deal. He was producing game shows — or trying to — and needed questions written. He called me at home and said, 'Here's the show. I need 25 questions.' I said, 'Great, how much are you going to pay me?' He said, 'Marc, it's Bob. Don't worry. I'll take care of you.'"
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Marc Summers attends "The Great Gatsby" Broadway opening night at Broadway Theatre on April 25, 2024, in New York City. (Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images)

"So I wanted to impress him," Summers continued. "Instead of giving him 25 questions, I gave him 50. I thought, 'Oh my God, this is going to be great.' I called him and said, 'Bob, let me come by the house and drop them off.' He said, 'No, no, just put them in the mailbox, and there'll be an envelope in there for you.' I wrote him 50 questions when he'd only asked for 25, hoping for a check for $400 or $500. There was a check made out to Marc Summers for the grand total of 50 bucks. So that's the way it was."
WATCH: FAMOUS GAME SHOW HOST BOB BARKER PASSES AWAY AT 99

In March, Holly Hallstrom claimed on "Dirty Rotten Scandals" that she lost her job on "The Price Is Right" after refusing to publicly stand by Barker when fellow model Dian Parkinson accused him of sexual harassment in a 1994 lawsuit. Hallstrom, one of the show's longtime "Barker's Beauties," said producers blamed her 1995 firing on weight gain caused by medication.
Barker consistently denied wrongdoing and maintained that any relationships were consensual. Fox News Digital reached out to Parkinson for comment.

From left: Holly Hallstrom, game show host Bob Barker and Janice Pennington attend the party to celebrate Pennington's book "Husband, Lover, Spy" on Jan. 13, 1994, at Spago in West Hollywood. Hallstrom was fired in 1995. (Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"When Dian filed her suit, oh boy, that was the beginning of when everything got really bad," Hallstrom told Fox News Digital. "I thought the whole situation, all the publicity, all the media attention, I thought it was horrible. I thought it was tacky. I was glad [co-creator] Mark Goodson had died [in 1992]. He would’ve been mortified to see that kind of tacky scandal on what was a family show."

"I didn't want to be involved in it at all," Hallstrom said. "Barker wanted us to go on all these talk shows and say he was the victim and that Dian was lying. I didn't participate because I thought it was tacky. I also couldn't honestly say, 'Oh yes, Dian is lying,' or 'Oh no, Dian is not lying.' I was not present for those conversations."
American model Dian Parkinson poses in a publicity photo for the CBS game show "The Price is Right" in Los Angeles, circa 1976. (CBS Photo Archive/Getty Images)

"I just avoided doing all of Bob’s PR tour," Hallstrom continued. "Finally, I was told I would be appearing on ‘The Suzanne Somers Show,’ period. And I did. Of course, all they wanted was for me to say that Dian was lying. When Suzanne asked me if I thought Dian was lying, I just babbled some answer, and that was that.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Janice Pennington, Holly Hallstrom, Dian Parkinson and Bob Barker are seen here during a taping of "The Price Is Right." (Everett)

"But then that week, I read in the tabloids, ‘Holly says, ‘Dian is lying.’ I never said that. I called the tabloid and demanded a retraction. They printed a retraction. But that was the beginning of the big rift between Bob and me. That’s when I got on his s--t list."
Parkinson dropped her lawsuit in 1995. At the time, her attorney said the legal battle had become too emotionally and financially draining and had begun affecting her physical health.

"Barker went all over television saying, ‘Her case was dismissed, and I’m totally vindicated,’" Hallstrom recalled. "I said, ‘That’s not true.’ I would not comment on that. I did not participate in those interviews. ... I would not change my testimony to suit Barker. That’s when I was told my weight was a problem. I was off the show."
Holly Hallstrom (above) was fired from "The Price Is Right" in 1995 after serving as one of "Barker's Beauties" for 18 years. (CBS via Getty Images)
"That was, well, probably the worst thing in my life at that point that had ever happened," Hallstrom admitted. "It only got worse from there."

Hallstrom and Barker spent nearly a decade locked in a legal battle after he sued her for defamation, according to Business Insider. She filed a countersuit alleging defamation, emotional distress and discrimination.

According to the outlet, Hallstrom said she was effectively blacklisted in the entertainment industry and pushed to the brink financially. She also declined settlement offers, saying she refused to be silenced by a nondisclosure agreement.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Holly Hallstrom claimed she was blacklisted after being fired from "The Price Is Right." (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

Two days before Hallstrom's case was scheduled to go to trial, Barker and CBS agreed to settle, Business Insider reported. According to the outlet, CBS agreed to pay Hallstrom a settlement reportedly worth millions. The terms were not disclosed, and the settlement did not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.

"I was not going to sign a nondisclosure for that show or anything," she said. "I was not going to sign away my right to free speech. It also meant that Barker could not do to me what he did to Dian, go out and claim victory and vindication. ... He could not say anything about me as long as I could speak out for myself. And he never said another word."
TV host Bob Barker is seen here arriving at the National Arts and Entertainment Journalism Awards Gala at Millennium Biltmore Hotel on Dec. 6, 2015, in Los Angeles. (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images)

Not everyone accepted the show's portrayal of Barker. His longtime publicist defended the late host as "beloved" and "the greatest MC in TV history," while longtime producer Roger Dobkowitz denounced the series as an "obvious hit piece," arguing "The Price Is Right" "was a happy place" for most employees.
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: 'American Idol' winner says husband 'put his badge up' to support her music career
summary: "American Idol" winner Hannah Harper says her husband left an eight-year law enforcement career to become her tour manager, a sacrifice she says strengthened their marriage.
story: "American Idol" 2026 champion Hannah Harper tells Fox News Digital about her husband's career sacrifice, why he traded his badge for the road and how it changed their marriage.
Hannah Harper says her husband made the ultimate career sacrifice to help launch her country music dreams.

The "American Idol" Season 24 winner exclusively revealed to Fox News Digital that her husband walked away from a nearly decade long career in law enforcement, "put his badge up" and joined her full-time on the road as her tour manager.
"It has definitely strengthened our marriage in ways that I didn't even know those muscles worked, if that makes sense," Harper said.
CARRIE UNDERWOOD SURPRISES 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT WITH TIFFANY JEWELRY AND HANDWRITTEN NOTE
"American Idol" winner Hannah Harper says her husband left law enforcement and put his police badge up to become her tour manager as her country music career took off. (Eric McCandless / Disney)

"My husband was in law enforcement for eight years and put his badge up just so that I could pursue this. And he was doing insurance there for a little while. We were going to try to just do, like, a work-on-the-road kind of thing. And then music just got too busy. And he was like, 'You know what? I think I want to be tour manager.' And I was like, 'That's perfect. I think you should do that.'"

The career pivot came as Harper's schedule exploded following her "American Idol" victory, leaving the couple searching for a way to keep their family together while managing an increasingly busy tour calendar.

Harper is currently on her first national tour and recently landed her first major brand partnership with Sargento after her original song, "String Cheese," went viral during her "American Idol" run. The cheese company is sponsoring her tour with a custom-wrapped bus stocked with snacks for Harper, her band, crew and family.
"American Idol" champion Hannah Harper is on her first national tour and recently landed her first major brand partnership with Sargento. (Sargento / Hannah Harper)
However, working side by side with her husband has sometimes come with its own growing pains, Harper pointed out.
CARRIE UNDERWOOD WARNS HOLLYWOOD IS A 'SELF-SERVING BUSINESS,' CREDITS FAITH FOR KEEPING HER GROUNDED

"I think the biggest challenge now is because we're both working is, ‘OK, when are off hours?' You know, like when normal people go home, they're done working for the day, but our work is at home. And so, it's hard for us to be able to turn it off. But it's so much fun for both of us to be building this together."
WATCH: ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ WINNER SAYS HUSBAND TRADED POLICE BADGE FOR MUSIC TOUR LIFE

Before being crowned the winner of "American Idol" Season 24, Harper was already building a life with her husband, Devon Mendenhall. The couple, who married in April 2018, welcomed their first son the following year and have since grown their family to include three boys.
Hannah Harper was crowned the winner of "American Idol" Season 24. (Eric McCandless / Disney)
Harper said the family's all-in approach has become one of the most rewarding parts of her success.
"My entire family is on the road with me, both of my brothers, my parents, my kids. And I think it's so special that everyone has a role and a job, and everyone feels included."
Sargento is sponsoring Harper's tour after her original song, "String Cheese," went viral during her "American Idol" run. (Sargento / Hannah Harper)
The singer became emotional, reflecting on her husband's sacrifice.

"But more than anything, I feel honored that he was willing to step down from his position. A lot of men wouldn't do that. I think their pride would get in the way, and that man would bend over backwards for anything that I asked him to do."
WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' WINNER CREDITS CARRIE UNDERWOOD FOR HELPING HER NAVIGATE FAME

As Harper adjusts to her rapid rise in country music, she said fellow "American Idol" winner, Carrie Underwood, offered advice that has helped her navigate the pressures of fame without losing herself.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Carrie, just saying like social media, the stage presence that one has to have, it's like a character basically, and you have to separate that character from reality, which is hard for me because I want them to be the same."
Carrie Underwood gave Hannah Harper some advice after she won "American Idol." ( Eric McCandless/Disney via Getty Images)

"I want everyone to feel connected to me and know that I'm real and authentic, but there definitely has to be a separation on my stage mask and mom, if that makes sense. And so, I'm learning that very quickly and how important it is to be able to take it off and still be Mom and still be the Hannah I was before 'American Idol.'"
Harper said one of the biggest surprises following her "American Idol" win was watching "String Cheese" take on a life of its own.
WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' WINNER REVEALS HOW VIRAL SONG KEEPS REOPENING HER DEEPEST WOUNDS
The deeply personal song, inspired by her experience with motherhood and postpartum depression, has become an anthem for parents who see themselves in its message.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"I am so emotionally connected to the people who are going through it," Harper said.
Hannah Harper performing on "American Idol" earlier this year. (Frank Micelotta/Disney)

"In meet-and-greet lines... there are at least 50 of those are women who walked the exact same path as I did when it came to postpartum depression or just being in the trenches of motherhood. And getting to connect with them during their hardships... I relive all of those same emotions while talking to them and it still feels fresh."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Harper believes the song's impact extends beyond music.

"And I think that it's a song that continues to give, and I didn't write it on my own. I think the Lord just kind of like laid it in my lap, and He's used it to minister to people as well as me."Harper will remain on the road through November for her first national tour, with upcoming stops across the country and appearances alongside Brad Paisley and Lauren Alaina.
Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: 'Baywatch' star Brandy Ledford shares fitness secrets at 57, says she's 'not ready to hang up my bikini yet'
summary: Brandy Ledford reveals her fitness routine now centers on heavy weight training for bone density and shares the beauty secrets behind her ageless look.
story: The actress reveals why strength training has become the foundation of her health, confidence and longevity. Ledford also weighs in on the upcoming "Baywatch" reboot and shares her advice for the new cast.
Brandy Ledford has no problem revealing the secrets behind her youthful glow.
The "Baywatch: Hawaii" alum said her beauty routine boils down to two Bs: "Botox and bleach."

The star, 57, who made hearts race as lifeguard Dawn Masterton, is hosting a luxury wellness retreat for women in September. She is also a creator on Passes, where she shares exclusive content and connects directly with fans.
JANE SEYMOUR, 75, SHARES HOW SHE APPROACHES AGING WITH VITALITY: 'BEST I CAN BE'
"Baywatch: Hawaii" alum Brandy Ledford, now a content creator on Passes, previously spoke to Fox News Digital about her sobriety journey. (Caroline Malouf)
Ledford told Fox News Digital that she has zero qualms about still being recognized as a sex symbol by fans today.
"I love, I mean, I'm a grandmother," she gushed. "I mean, what? That's so great! I think it's so fun. I'm not ready to hang up my bikini yet."
As she has gotten older, Ledford said her fitness philosophy has evolved.
Brandy Ledford doesn't mind being called a sex symbol. (Courtesy of Brandy Ledford)

"My fitness routine these days focuses on strength training more than ever," she said. "When you get to be my age, you need to lift weights for bone density and longevity. My doctor is really stressing weight training using heavier weights for me."
WATCH: ‘BAYWATCH: HAWAII’ ALUM BRANDY LEDFORD REVEALS HER FITNESS SECRETS
"For the last few years, I was pretty addicted to yoga sculpt, a high-intensity yoga workout with light weights. I'm really trying to use much heavier weights now to strengthen my bones and muscles."
"I also still love walking, and I still love yoga," Ledford said. "I love to go on hikes. But I'd say right now, I'm really, really, really focused on serious weight training."
Brandy Ledford still does yoga daily, along with weightlifting, to look and feel her best. (Courtesy of Brandy Ledford)
Ledford's commitment to fitness is not new. Looking back, she said landing "Baywatch" required her to kick one unhealthy habit.
WATCH: ‘BAYWATCH’ STAR BRANDY LEDFORD SAYS FAITH HELPED TRANSFORM HER SOBRIETY JOURNEY

"I'm a really good swimmer," she said. "I'm from the beach, so we grew up swimming in the ocean. But at the time, I was a smoker, and there were stamina tests. They would throw quarters to the bottom of the deep end of the pool, and you'd have to swim down. They wanted to see how long you could hold your breath. It was kind of hard for me at the time, so I quit smoking."
Brandy Ledford gave up smoking after she was cast in "Baywatch." (Courtesy of Brandy Ledford)
"I did end up getting a lot better at holding my breath underwater and became a lot better at swimming," she added.
Ledford also "hired a trainer immediately" to make sure she always looked swimsuit-ready for every scene.
Brandy Ledford is seen here as Dawn Masterton in "Baywatch: Hawaii." (ZUMA Press Inc./ALAMY)

"He trained me in the water and got me really comfortable working and exercising in the water," she said. "Then I worked out with weights. I also did a lot of workouts in the sand. The sand is an incredible workout. Even walking in the sand is a great workout. And when we got to Hawaii, we worked out at the gym there."

"I just trained a lot," she said. "I really wanted to be comfortable in my swimsuit and not be self-conscious. I think that shows. When you're self-conscious, it shows. So I wanted to feel comfortable, and the only way I knew how was to work out and take care of my body."
Brandy Ledford is a yoga teacher who splits her time between Los Angeles, Vancouver and Kauai. (Caroline Malouf)

"We all made it a priority to get our workouts in and swim in the ocean. Walking from our trailer to the set in the sand was a workout in itself. That was really important to me, and it became part of my lifestyle. I've actually maintained it to this day."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Today, Brandy Ledford is also a wellness advocate. (Courtesy of Brandy Ledford)
Ledford noted she still works out daily to look and feel her best.

"I think health is our greatest wealth," Ledford said. "I really believe that what you feel on the inside is going to come out on the outside. I've been sober for 14 years, and that's been a big life changer. I have a really strong faith in God. Listen, I do all the things, but it starts from the inside. I love really good skincare. I think healthy hair is a big part of it. And I think a beautiful smile is important. I'm always drinking water."
Brandy Ledford and Carmen Electra attend the 33rd Annual Race To Erase MS Gala at Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles, Calif., on June 5, 2026. (Getty Images for Race to Erase MS)
The actress said maintaining her appearance involves more than workouts and beauty treatments.
Brandy Ledford told Fox News Digital she continues to lean on her personal relationship with God after getting sober. (Matt Kallish)

"I value what I look like on the outside because I value so much of the work I do on the inside," Ledford said. "I always say I do so much work in my inner life. The second I get up, I'm in prayer and meditation. I want to look as good on the outside as I feel on the inside, so I make it a priority. But I'm just as comfortable with no makeup, sweats, a hoodie and my fluffy slippers."
Ledford said she's feeling so good these days that she's even tempted to pull out her "Baywatch" swimsuit and rock it again.
Brandy Ledford attends the 30th anniversary of "Baywatch" at the Viceroy Hotel in Santa Monica, California, on Sept. 24, 2019. (Presley Ann/Getty Images)

"It's in storage somewhere," she said. "I might pull it out and do a photo shoot in it. It was pretty iconic — yellow — because red is what's known as the 'Baywatch' one-piece. But in 'Baywatch: Hawaii,' we wore yellow because it came from the Australian lifeguards. They wear yellow. It's not an easy color to pull off, but we had so much body makeup on that it all looked good."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Brandy Ledford and Jason Brooks are seen here in Hawaii on June 1, 1999. (ZUMA Press, Inc.)
Ledford said she's excited to check out the new "Baywatch" reboot, which stars Brooks Nader, Shay Mitchell and Livvy Dunne, among others.

"The advice I'd give the ladies to look glamorous and effortless on the beach in all those scenes is to stay hydrated, wear sunscreen, work out and feel comfortable in your body. They're all so beautiful, fit and in great shape. Every one of those girls looks amazing."
Brandy Ledford made her film debut opposite Sylvester Stallone in the 1993 action hit "Demolition Man." (Matt Kallish)

"I think we tend to look back at our younger selves and say, 'I wish I'd known how cute I was. I wish I'd realized I looked good in that bikini.' So just know that you look amazing and let it shine from the inside."
Brandy Ledford attends the premiere of ABC News Studios docuseries "After Baywatch: Moment in the Sun" at The Bungalow on Aug. 26, 2024, in Santa Monica, California. (Variety via Getty Images)
Ledford said she isn't surprised "Baywatch" is still making a splash decades later.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Brandy Ledford attends the 6th Jam For Janie Grammy Awards Viewing Party presented by Live Nation at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles, on Feb. 2, 2025. (Getty Images for Janie's Fund)

"First of all, it's iconic," she said. "It's a fantasy. People got to escape. The men were hot, and the women were beautiful. But there was also drama and really good action. It was just the perfect show. I think we need that in our lives again these days."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Kelsey Grammer admits surprising reason 'Frasier' almost never happened
summary: Kelsey Grammer reveals a dinner with Paramount's president changed his post-"Cheers" plans and led to the creation of the iconic "Frasier" spinoff.
story: Kelsey Grammer reflects on starring in "Young Washington" and explains why he believes the Founding Fathers' vision still offers guidance for America's future.
Kelsey Grammer is revealing the surprising twist that turned "Frasier" into one of television's most successful sitcoms.
The actor recently appeared on "Planet Tyrus," where he revealed he nearly starred in a different show after "Cheers" before one conversation changed everything.
Grammer spent nine seasons portraying the Boston psychiatrist on "Cheers," where the character evolved from Diane Chambers' love interest to one of the bar's most memorable regulars.
KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS
Kelsey Grammer starred as Dr. Frasier Crane on NBC's "Frasier" for 11 seasons, from 1993 to 2004. (Gale Adler/Paramount)

"It’s funny, I had visions," the star explained. "I’d been offered another show. They said, ‘We want to do a show with you when "Cheers" is over.’ They said, ‘We think you could actually carry a show on your own.’ I said, ‘Great.’ So we actually started doing it with the same writers that ended up on 'Frasier.' We wrote a completely different story, and they wrote a script. I thought it was kind of funny."
Kelsey Grammer as Dr. Frasier Crane and Ted Danson as Sam Malone. (NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

"I went out for dinner with John Pike, who was the president of Paramount at the time," the 71-year-old shared. "... I said, 'Have you read the script?' He said, 'Yeah. And I think a sitcom should be funny. ... This is what you guys have come up with? I don't like it. I think you should play Frasier.'"
"It was John Pike who said, 'Play Frasier.’"
WATCH: KELSEY GRAMMER SHARES THE KEY TO ACHIEVING THE 'AMERICAN DREAM'
Grammer was listening.
"I said, ‘OK, I see what you’re saying. Build an audience. I am kind of funny in the character. He can’t be married anymore, and he can’t have kids,’" Grammer said.

"He did have a son. ... My thing about sitcoms is if there's a child in it, the child growing up every year becomes the most interesting thing about the show. ... Becoming a young woman or becoming a young man is the only really interesting thing that's going on in front of you. So I got rid of that, had him come in once in a while."

From left: Bebe Neuwirth as Dr. Lilith Sternin, Trevor Einhorn as Frederick Gaylord Crane and Kelsey Grammer as Dr. Frasier Crane appear in "The Apparent Trap," episode 9 of "Frasier." (NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

Grammer said moving Frasier from Boston to Seattle helped separate the spinoff from "Cheers." It also gave a believable reason why his young son, Frederick, wasn't part of the show full-time instead of making the psychiatrist seem like a "deadbeat dad."
"[I] just had to be a man trying to find his way," said Grammer.
"Whose support payments were on time," Tyrus joked.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Emmy winners Kelsey Grammer and David Hyde Pierce join fellow "Frasier" cast members Jane Leeves, Peri Gilpin, John Mahoney and Dan Butler for a group hug backstage at the 50th Annual Emmy Awards on Sept. 13, 1998, in Los Angeles. (Bob Riha, Jr./Getty Images)

"Frasier" premiered on Sept. 16, 1993, and ran for 11 seasons before ending on May 13, 2004. The sitcom won 37 Primetime Emmy Awards and drew 25.2 million viewers for its series finale, becoming one of television's most acclaimed comedies.

In 2023, Grammer reprised his iconic role in the "Frasier" revival on Paramount+, which followed the psychiatrist's return to Boston. The series ran for two seasons before Paramount+ canceled it in 2025.
Noticeably absent from the reboot was John Mahoney, who played Grammer’s on-screen father, Martin Crane. Mahoney died in 2018 at 77.
Actor John Mahoney died on Feb. 4, 2018, at the age of 77. (Margaret C. Norton/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images via Getty Images)

"John was a remarkably fun guy," Grammer told Fox News Digital in 2021. "He was always kind and sweet and lovely. But the ironic thing about him — when I was directing him once on the show, I said, ‘John, let’s put the dog Eddie in your lap.’ And he says, ‘No, no.’ I said, ‘What’s going on?’ ‘He always bites me. He always growls at me. He scares me, and I don’t like it.’ So I thought, ‘Oh, this is weird. I had no idea.’"
Kelsey Grammer attends the "Frasier" SAG Screening Event on Sept. 9, 2024, in West Hollywood. (Randy Shropshire/Getty Images for Paramount+)

"So they had to put a little sardine oil on his hands, so the dog would lick something instead of trying to growl at him or bite him. This love for Eddie that existed on the show really wasn’t real. It was just an on-camera love. They fought each other, and he was really funny about his relationship with the dog."

"... Every time I spoke to him, we just had a great time," Grammer continued. "We spent time in New York together off-screen, and I saw him in Chicago, and I saw him in Ireland once. He was just a wonderful guy."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Pictured from left: Kelsey Grammer as Dr. Frasier Crane, Moose as Eddie, John Mahoney as Martin Crane and David Hyde Pierce as Dr. Niles Crane. (NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
At the time, Grammer said he was eager for what the future held, both personally and professionally.

"You know what? Life always inspired me," he said. "Life and the variety of experience is what inspires me. People inspire me; I love people. I mean, it’s odd that I ended up on a show that was based in a bar. My favorite places on Earth are bars. I’ve had the best experiences, met the most interesting people in bars around the world. And so, what keeps me going personally is that there is always another experience I haven’t known."
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Kelsey Grammer attends a special screening of Paramount+'s "Frasier" Season 2 at Bluma Appel Theatre in Toronto, Ontario, on Sept. 19, 2024. (Mathew Tsang/Getty Images)

"... I'll go right up to the edge before it starts to get dangerous," he joked. "But I love it. I love riding horses, I love shooting guns, I love just exploring all the things that people can do and all the things that a character can do and show you. By virtue of the fact that you've played it, you've actually kind of lived it."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Marilyn Monroe role leaves actresses 'set up to fail': experts
summary: Branding experts explain why Marilyn Monroe remains Hollywood's most untouchable icon and why every actress who portrays her seems set up to fail.
story: Melissa Stevens, granddaughter of late photographer Sam Shaw, discusses the new book, "Dear Marilyn: The Unseen Letters and Photographs."
Dakota Johnson's reported turn as Marilyn Monroe is already reigniting a familiar Hollywood debate: Can anyone successfully step into the shoes of one of the world's most enduring cultural icons?
Instead of a traditional biopic, Maggie Gyllenhaal's "Flesh Impact" imagines Monroe beyond the platinum hair and red lipstick, exploring the woman behind one of pop culture's most enduring personas.

Branding experts say the reaction is part of a decades-long pattern. Every generation produces another actress willing to portray Monroe, but few escape comparisons to the Hollywood icon, whose glamour, mystique and tragic legacy have made her one of the entertainment industry's most untouchable figures. The fresh premise did little to quiet critics online, many of whom argued Hollywood should stop revisiting Monroe altogether.
"i think we have enough movies about her," a social media user wrote online as a first look of Johnson was shared.
DAKOTA JOHNSON STUNS AS MARILYN MONROE IN FIRST LOOK AFTER DIRECTOR DOUBTED CASTING

More than six decades after her death, Marilyn Monroe remains one of Hollywood's most enduring cultural icons, with experts saying the actress's legacy makes her one of the industry's most difficult figures to portray. (Baron/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)
"Please leave Marilyn alone," another added. "Let her rest in peace."
"How many f---ing times y'all gonna reheat the Marilyn Monroe nachos supreme?" one user questioned.

The backlash doesn't come as a surprise to branding experts, who say Monroe occupies a rare place in American pop culture that makes her one of Hollywood's most difficult figures to portray. Decades after her death, they argue, audiences still feel a personal connection to the screen legend.

"Marilyn Monroe is this irreplaceable icon that embodied glamor, mystique and tragedy. We all feel like we know Marilyn Monroe and any actress that portrays her almost seems like an imposter," strategic communications expert Kelcey Kintner explained to Fox News Digital. "So it's almost as if these actresses are set up to fail, even thought it's an incredibly dynamic person to play."

Dakota Johnson's reported casting as Marilyn Monroe in the upcoming film "Flesh Impact" has sparked debate online, with some fans questioning whether Hollywood should revisit the late screen legend. (Courtesy of Genesis)
One expert likened modern Monroe portrayals to an overcomplicated twist on a classic.

"Ever go to a restaurant and hear the server say ’this is the chef’s take on a cheeseburger’ but you don’t want an interpretation, you just want a cheeseburger?" branding expert Doug Eldridge told Fox News Digital.
"It’s Res Ipsa Loquitur. ‘The thing speaks for itself,’" he explained. "The same holds true for other iconic staples, such as Marilyn Monroe: often imitated, never duplicated."
MARILYN MONROE'S ICONIC SUBWAY GRATE PHOTO HAS SURPRISING WWII ROOTS AND HIDDEN HISTORY
Dakota Johnson will play Marilyn Monroe at age 36 in "Flesh Impact." (Matt Winkelmeyer/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images)

Hollywood's continued fascination with Monroe is symptomatic of a much larger problem: an industry increasingly driven by reboots, remakes and familiar intellectual property rather than original storytelling.

"Paradoxically, Hollywood is often thought to be the home of ‘creativity’ yet much of the content being produced these days, hinges on reboots and extensions of past successes," Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, said. "How deep are we in the comic book catalog at this point – producers are chasing that lightning in the bottle moment, but it comes with fatigue; it starts with sagging box office numbers, but eventually, it ends when viewers become ambivalent and ratings head off a cliff."
"Creating something fresh and truly unique is an incredibly difficult endeavor, but rehashing the same narrative and storyline also comes at a price."

Marilyn Monroe's glamour, mystique and enduring cultural legacy continue to inspire new film projects, even as each portrayal draws intense scrutiny from fans and critics alike. (M. Garrett/Murray Garrett/Getty Images)

"In our age of AI and technology, it draws back to a simpler time when Hollywood icons could command so much singular attention," Kintner, Senior VP at Red Banyan PR, explained. title: 'Criminal Minds' star Mandy Patinkin shares unconventional plan for after his death
summary: Mandy Patinkin revealed why his claustrophobia and Jewish heritage connected to Auschwitz make both burial and cremation unacceptable options.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Mandy Patinkin decided that when he dies, he wants his body to be composted.

The 73-year-old said on his "Don't Listen to Us" podcast that he remembered memorizing a speech from "Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead, "and it was about being in a box … But the idea — I'm very claustrophobic, very claustrophobic, and the idea of being put in a box, knowing that I'm going to be in a box when whatever I'm familiar with is drastically changed is just unacceptable to me. Period. Full stop."
The "Criminal Minds" star continued, "Don't give me any business about, 'Well, you're not you, you're not here, it's a whole different thing.' Excuse me. Not OK."
NICOLE KIDMAN PLANS ON BECOMING A DEATH DOULA AS SHE ADMITS IT 'MAY SOUND A LITTLE WEIRD'
Mandy Patinkin shared his end-of-life plans on his podcast this week. (Getty Images for National Dance Institute)

And because of his Jewish heritage, he explained, "The other idea of being put in an oven is seared into my heritage genetics of the crematorium in Auschwitz, which I've visited. I can't bear the idea of being burned."

He said that while he considers himself a "conservative Chicago Jew," Orthodox Judaism dictates that "you must not do anything. You must not even let somebody do an autopsy on your body to study something, because when you go to the Olam Haba, the world beyond, you must be complete, because when the Messiah comes and everything is resurrected, and the Jews are waiting for that … you must be complete."
Patinkin joked that "you'll be in the 'Wizard of Oz' looking for the parts" otherwise.
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Mandy Patinkin starred as Jason Gideon in "Criminal Minds." (CBS via Getty Images)

"I can't deal with the oven and I can't deal with the box," he said. "I love this idea so much because I don't have to be burned, and I don't have to be claustrophobic. I'm naturally put in this encasement that you've just described. I'm free to go to the Olam Haba, the world beyond, as complete. And then the organic process turns me into, you know, mulch, food, soil. And I'm not in an oven … I just am ecstatic over this."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
The CEO of a human composting facility in Auburn, Washington, is seen doing a demonstration in 2019. (AFP via Getty Images)
Patinkin was presented with the idea by a woman named Robyn who came on to his podcast to discuss her husband’s wish for an earth-friendly burial.

Human composting involves putting a person’s body inside a vessel and covering it in organic material. The vessel breaks down the body through controlled heat, oxygen and moisture over a period of about a month, eventually becoming soil that is returned to the family.

title: 'Fire Country' star Diane Farr leaves Los Angeles after 30 years to start her 'third act'
summary: Diane Farr shared an emotional Instagram video documenting her last day in Los Angeles after exactly 30 years, calling the move harder than expected.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
"Fire Country" star Diane Farr has left Los Angeles after 30 years.
The 56-year-old actress took to Instagram to share snippets from her "Last Day in LA," noting she has lived in the city for "exactly 30 years" and that "more importantly- I chose LA."

"I wasn’t born here, I didn’t go to school here - I just had a chance for representation as an actor and I moved out of NYC the summer I was 26," she wrote. "I came like most of the people I love in Hollywoodland - none of which I saw this week bc moving sucks."
She went on to say that she came to Los Angeles "chasing a dream that I am still shocked worked out."
The actress shared she is leaving Los Angeles after 30 years of living there. (Bob D'Amico/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’

Farr's acting career began in the '90s, with the actress landing her breakthrough role in "Roswell" in 1999. She later earned leading roles in "Numb3rs," "Splitting Up Together" and, most recently, "Fire Country."
In addition to her acting career, Farr also reflected on the many other positive experiences she had while living in Los Angeles, including starting a family.

"I also got to raise babies in the sun and the mountains and enjoy this beautiful home and attend public schools ??" she said. "Pinch me I’m overwhelmed by the blessings and hope, really hope I gave enough back. LA will always be where my family is from."
Farr shares three children with her ex-husband, Seung Yong Chung: son Beckett, 18, and twin daughters Coco and Sawyer, 17.

"We are just taking a hiatus now - a word I learned here - so we are letting the house go," she concluded her caption. "But god damn this was harder than I thought. To leave this house. To leave this dream, even if it is realized - and to leave home. Thank you #cityofangels."
Many fans took to the comments section to wish the actress good luck in the next chapter of her life, with one writing, "Good luck and safe travels as you start the next book in your series of life."

title: Monica Lewinsky has one request for critics nearly 30 years after White House scandal
summary: Monica Lewinsky wishes critics would get new jokes after nearly three decades, sharing on a podcast how she reshaped public perception of her own story.
story: Activist Monica Lewinsky told Fox News Digital that her personal definition of power has evolved over the years.
Monica Lewinsky has evolved since the White House scandal – and she hopes critics one day can, too.
Lewinsky, 53, credited time and patience as her saving graces while reflecting on challenges from her past during an appearance on the "All the Cool Girls" podcast.
"I think that coming into my 50s was amazing and just the shedding of worries," she told co-hosts Laura Brown and Kristina O'Neill.
MONICA LEWINSKY'S LINDSEY GRAHAM TRIBUTE DRAWS CRITICISM AND PRAISE FOR PLACING PEOPLE OVER PARTY: EXPERT
Monica Lewinsky reclaimed her own narrative years after a White House scandal. (Monica Schipper)

"I mean that whole … joke about 'I don't give anymore f---s,' and it's like you really start to give fewer and fewer f---s, and you settle into acceptance in a way that has been really reassuring for me."
Unlike the critics, the podcast host moved on from past discretions to reclaim not only her life, but also her own story.
"In terms of the people who still have old, old beliefs, I wish they would get some new jokes because, I mean, 30 years of the same jokes, Jesus," she said. "Or 28 years. We're not at 30 yet."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Monica Lewinsky pleaded for critics to find a new joke nearly 30 years after her highly-publicized scandal. (Amy Sussman/Getty Images)

Lewinsky was 21 years old when she began an unpaid internship at the White House in July 1995. She turned 22 that summer, and her sexual relationship with former President Bill Clinton, who was 49 at the time, began in November 1995.

It was only after she confided in a Pentagon co-worker, Linda Tripp – who secretly recorded their conversations, which were then used in Paula Jones' sexual harassment lawsuit against Clinton – when the affair became public fodder.

During a January 1998 White House news conference, Clinton famously denied the affair, and stated, "I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky," and Lewinsky subsequently went into hiding due to public humiliation.
Bill Clinton was impeached while serving as the 42nd president. (House Judiciary Committee/Getty Images)

The subsequent impeachment trial against the 42nd president began in January 1999 and ended Feb. 12. While Clinton was impeached by the house, he was acquitted of perjury and obstruction of justice charges.
While the scandal made headlines for years, Lewinsky only truly began reclaiming her identity in the last decade.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I feel really grateful. I'm really grateful, and I'm excited," she said. "It's when I step away, and I look at my own story objectively – or as objectively as one can – it is pretty extraordinary to still be here, like physically still here, and to have been able to help shape how people see me more and understand me more and connect with me in ways that are meaningful. It's bonkers."
Monica Lewinsky previously recalled the toll of receiving negative energy from "billions of strangers" over the years. (Robin L. Marshall)
Themes surrounding authority and control have remained a constant in Lewinsky's life post scandal.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I think of power in two different ways. There's the power that someone has and they use, that impacts other people's power," Lewinsky explained to Fox News Digital earlier this year.
"Then there's the power that someone has in connection to themselves and that's a lot more like strength."

She added, "People often think of resilience as being linear, and it is so much more like a spiral. You will move forward, you'll go back, and move forward ... you'll go back, and I think it's, again, people have to be patient with themselves."

title: Ryan Gosling's family-first philosophy reshaped his Hollywood career: experts
summary: From "Barbie" to "Ghost Rider," Ryan Gosling's pivot toward blockbuster franchises traces back to a deliberate family-first philosophy he embraced as a dad.
story: Ryan Gosling and Sandra Hüller on epic adventure, science included, theme of being brave with challenging projects and how Goslings space wardrobe is a "love letter" to the late Val Kilmer in "Real Genius"
Ryan Gosling is officially joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider, marking the latest chapter in a career evolution that the actor has linked directly to fatherhood.

Earlier this month, Gosling, 45, made a surprise appearance during Marvel Studios' panel at San Diego Comic-Con where it was announced that he will be starring as the titular motorcycle-riding supernatural hero in a standalone "Ghost Rider" movie slated for release in 2028.

Gosling's casting comes as the three-time Oscar nominee continues to embrace blockbuster franchises after spending years building his reputation in some of Hollywood's darkest, most critically acclaimed dramas.
MARVEL STAR VINCENT D’ONOFRIO SAYS HE ‘CAN’T DO’ KINGPIN TRANSFORMATION ANYMORE
Ryan Gosling's family-first philosophy sparked his career evolution, according to experts. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images)

The actor has previously shared that his pivot toward lighter, more mainstream projects was intentional, explaining that his priorities changed after becoming a parent. Gosling shares daughters Esmeralda, 11, and Amada, 10, with his longtime partner, Eva Mendes, 52.
During a 2024 interview with The Wall Street Journal, Gosling said he avoids psychologically heavy roles because he wants to be emotionally present for Mendes and their daughters.

"I don’t really take roles that are going to put me in some kind of dark place," Gosling said. "This moment is what I feel like trying to read the room at home and feel like what is going to be best for all of us. The decisions I make, I make them with Eva, and we make them with our family in mind first."
‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR SADIE ROBERTSON HUFF ADMITS ‘FEARS’ OVER PUTTING HER KIDS ON REALITY TV
While speaking with Fox News Digital, PR expert Sarah Schmidt shared her view that Gosling's family-first approach has reshaped not only the types of roles he is taking, but the purpose behind them.
"He began picking lighter roles to keep his mood stable for his family and also create art that they can be a part of," the president of Interdependence PR said.
Gosling spent years building his reputation in critically acclaimed dramas before becoming a blockbuster leading man. (Lloyd Bishop/NBC via Getty Images)
Paul Dergarabedian, head of Marketplace Trends for Rentrak, said Gosling's evolving priorities reflect a broader pattern among actors whose careers change alongside their personal lives.

"It does feel as though he is gravitating toward movies that his kids could actually see and enjoy," Dergarabedian said. "That kind of evolution is not unique as we have seen it with other actors as they get older, start families, and begin making choices that reflect where they are in life, how they see the world, and how they want to be perceived both personally and professionally."

Gosling's shift toward family-friendly entertainment signals a full-circle career moment for the actor, who made his debut as a child performer on the Disney Channel's "The All-New Mickey Mouse Club." He later appeared in the children's TV shows "Are You Afraid of the Dark?" and "Goosebumps."

During a 2011 interview with The New York Times, Gosling recalled that he decided to pursue "serious acting" at age 19. After making his mainstream breakthrough in the hit 2004 romantic drama "The Notebook," the Canada native went on to establish himself as one of Hollywood's most respected dramatic actors with critically acclaimed films, including "Half Nelson," "Blue Valentine," "Drive," "The Place Beyond the Pines," "Blade Runner 2049" and "First Man."
Gosling shares daughters Esmeralda and Amada with his longtime partner, Eva Mendes, who he met on the set of "The Place Beyond the Pines." (Sonia Recchia/Getty Images)

In recent years, Gosling has charted a different course with starring roles in audience-friendly movies including "Barbie," "The Fall Guy," and "Project Hail Mary," and his upcoming turns in "Star Wars: Starfighter" and "Ghost Rider."
Ryan McCormick, co-founder of Goldman McCormick PR, said he believes Gosling has earned the creative freedom to balance blockbuster franchises with prestige films.

"Ryan has not only built a career of acclaimed roles, those films are often box office successes," McCormick told Fox News Digital. "He has attained a rare status where he can do a sandbox film like 'Ghost Rider' and also take a dramatic or independent role without any one performance limiting his future choices."
Dergarabedian noted that Gosling's career has long defied easy categorization, citing his performances in 2011's "Crazy, Stupid, Love" and 2016's "La La Land."
"Gosling has always been far more versatile than any single role would suggest," Dergarabedian said. "He has shown he can do comedy, as he did so memorably in ‘Crazy, Stupid, Love.'"
"Of course, he proved he could carry a musical with ‘La La Land,'" he added.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Gosling said that "La La Land" was the first project he chose because of his children. (Dale Robinette/Lionsgate)

Dergarabedian pointed to Gosling's starring role in Nicolas Winding Refn's "Drive" as a pivotal moment that expanded audiences' perception of him beyond romantic leads and demonstrated his ability to tackle darker, action-oriented material.

"You really cannot put Gosling in a box. He has been able to move between genres and tones with a level of ease that very few actors can match," Dergarabedian said. "All that being said, you can definitely see a shift in tone at this stage of his career."

Gosling previously shared that "La La Land" was the first project he chose that reflected his changing priorities after becoming a father. While speaking with The Wall Street Journal, Gosling recalled thinking of how Esmeralda and Amada would enjoy watching him prepare for the role.
"It was just sort of like, ‘Oh, this will be fun for them, too, because even though they’re not coming to set, we’re practicing piano every day, or we’re dancing, or we’re singing,'" Gosling said.
The philosophy carried over to 2023's "Barbie," which Gosling said resonated with his daughters, who were already immersed in the world of Barbie dolls before he signed on to play Ken.

"Their interest in Barbie and their disinterest in Ken was an inspiration," Gosling said. "I thought they were already making little movies about their Barbies on the iPad when it happened, so the fact that I was going off to work to make one too, we just felt like we were aligned."
The actor said his daughters inspired him to star in "Barbie." (Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures)

Though some fans initially criticized Gosling's casting as Ken, arguing he was too old to portray Barbie's iconic counterpart, the actor ultimately won over audiences with a performance that became one of the film's biggest highlights. "Barbie" went on to gross more than $1.4 billion worldwide and Gosling earned an Oscar nomination for best supporting actor, cementing the film as both a commercial and critical triumph.
Schmidt told Fox News Digital that she believes the film fundamentally changed the trajectory of Gosling's career.
"Gosling proved that just because he began his career as a critically acclaimed darling does not mean that he cannot also be an international franchise and blockbuster star," she said.

"'Barbie' paved the way," Schmidt continued. "Prior to that, Gosling was a serious actor who occasionally moonlighted in a rom-com. As it turns out, Ken can carry a billion-dollar movie. He was funny and self-aware, and it did not cost him any of his hard-earned credibility."

Gosling has continued to embrace projects that his daughters can share with him. While promoting "Project Hail Mary," he revealed that Esmeralda and Amada occasionally voiced his alien co-star Rocky during rehearsals and became some of the sci-fi adventure movie's earliest viewers.
Gosling said his daughters helped him by sometimes voicing Rocky when he was filming "Project Hail Mary." (Jonathan Olley © 2026 Amazon Content Services LLC. All Rights Reserved.)

"Sometimes when I was working, and I needed to sort of switch things up or whatever, my kids would come in, and I had an earpiece in my ear, and they would talk for Rocky, so I could talk to them as Rocky," Gosling told People in March.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"And there's some moments in the movie where I'm laughing or I'm just so charmed by him, which is like, it's actually my kids talking to me and helping me out," Gosling continued.
"They've seen many cuts of this film," he added of his daughters. "They've given me many notes."

Marvel's "Ghost Rider" marks the latest chapter in the blockbuster era that Gosling has spent years building. Gosling's role as Johnny Blaze/Ghost Rider in the superhero movie will also reunite him with director Shawn Levy after the two previously collaborated on "Star Wars: Starfighter," which hits theaters in May 2027.
"Wow, is this really happening?" Gosling told the crowd at Comic-Con after being unveiled as Ghost Rider by Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige.
"As you know, this is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time," he said.
Gosling is starring in Marvel's "Ghost Rider," which will be released in 2028. (Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney)
Schmidt told Fox News Digital that she believes Gosling has found a way to balance artistic credibility with commercial success without losing sight of the priorities that reshaped his career.
"He became a dad first, actor second," Schmidt said. "He is building a filmography legacy that his kids can be part of and proud of."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Meanwhile, Dergarabedian said he believes Gosling's recent choices have also cemented his place among Hollywood's biggest stars.

"He has become a go-to actor for huge, audience-friendly studio films and major franchises because he occupies such a unique position within the public eye," Dergarabedian said. "He has credibility, he has charm, he has range, and he has that elusive movie-star quality that is increasingly rare today."
Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Kate Middleton is 'indispensable' to royal family as slimmed-down monarchy faces mounting pressure: expert
summary: Royal expert Katie Nicholl calls Kate Middleton "the monarchy's greatest asset," revealing how her cancer journey forged a deeper bond with King Charles.
story: Katie Nicholl, Vanity Fair royal correspondent and co-host of "The Royals Uncensored," says the Princess of Wales won public respect through duty and resilience after health challenges.
Kate Middleton has become one of King Charles' most beloved family members, with one royal expert calling her the "monarchy's greatest asset."

The claim came from Vanity Fair royal correspondent Katie Nicholl, co-host of "The Royals Uncensored." After more than 20 years covering the royal family on tours and engagements, Nicholl said she has spoken to countless palace insiders, many of whom are enchanted by the Princess of Wales.

"I think Catherine, the Princess of Wales, has always been a very valuable asset to the royal family," Nicholl told Fox News Digital. "She is the commoner who married into the royal family ... [She has made] a seamless transition into that unique world of royalty. It's not easy ... There's a huge amount of sacrifice that goes into being a member of the royal family."
PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FINALLY FEEL FREE TO SHOW AFFECTION IN PUBLIC: EXPERTS

King Charles III kisses Catherine, Princess of Wales, after the Requiem Mass for the Duchess of Kent at Westminster Cathedral in London on Sept. 16, 2025. Royal experts told Fox News Digital the touching moment reflects the increasingly close relationship the monarch shares with his daughter-in-law. (Jordan Pettitt - Pool/Getty Images)
"Catherine's had to give up a huge amount, and yet she does it all with a great deal of grace and dignity, always with a smile," Nicholl said. "So she is absolutely the monarchy's greatest asset."
Nicholl also noted that "the king adores her, and the queen adores her."

Catherine, Princess of Wales speaks with children during an official welcome at the Town Hall on the first day of her visit to Reggio Emilia on May 13, 2026, in Reggio Emilia, Italy. (UK Press via Getty Images)

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that Charles and Kate have forged an even deeper bond since both were diagnosed with cancer. Buckingham Palace announced the king's diagnosis in 2024. In December 2025, Charles shared the "good news" that his treatment would be scaled back in 2026.
WATCH: KATE MIDDLETON IS 'THE MONARCHY'S GREATEST ASSET: EXPERT'

Just weeks after the king's announcement, Kate revealed in March 2024 that she was undergoing treatment for an undisclosed form of cancer. She completed chemotherapy that September and announced in January 2025 that she was in remission.
British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that the king, 77, had been greatly inspired by the Princess of Wales' strength.
Catherine, Princess of Wales, Princess Charlotte of Wales and King Charles III during Trooping the Colour on June 15, 2024, in London. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

"King Charles sees enormous value in Princess Catherine," Chard said. "Not just as the wife of his heir, but as the cornerstone of the monarchy itself. He genuinely loves his 'darling' daughter-in-law. His face lights up when he is with her. They share similar interests, and they have shared a similar cancer journey, one that has created a deep bond and understanding that goes beyond duty."

King Charles III and Catherine, Princess of Wales, are seen here at the state banquet for German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife, Elke Budenbender, at Windsor Castle in Windsor, England, on Dec. 3, 2025. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)
Chard argued that it hasn't just been Charles who quickly realized that Kate represented the monarchy's future.
"The late queen saw it too," Chard said. "She recognized Catherine's superpowers early on — her ability to listen, find solutions and bring calm to difficult situations."
Queen Elizabeth II, England's longest-reigning monarch, died in 2022 at age 96. (Geoff Pugh)

"King Charles fundamentally views his time on the throne as stewardship," she said. "He sees himself as the caretaker of the institution and is acutely conscious of preparing the next generation. Collaborative preparation between the king and his heir is essential. Having Princess Catherine as the wife of his heir, Charles has struck gold."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, Princess Charlotte, Prince George and Prince Louis watch an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace after attending Trooping the Colour 2026 on June 13, 2026, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Royal author Sally Bedell Smith previously told People magazine that Kate is "like the daughter he never had."
"He has always had a very strong bond with her," Smith told the outlet. "He shares with William an impulse to protect her. They are in this together, Kate and the king."

Kate Middleton and the former Prince Charles examine artwork produced on silk during a visit to the Dulwich Picture Gallery on March 15, 2012, in Dulwich, south London, England. (John Stillwell - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
When Kate made her diagnosis public, Buckingham Palace said Charles was "so proud of Catherine for her courage in speaking as he did."

Catherine, Princess of Wales congratulates patient Claire Lorente and her partner, Pablo, as she rings the end-of-treatment bell at the Christie cancer care hospital in Manchester, England, on June 4, 2026. (Andy Stenning - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Author Christopher Andersen previously wrote in his book "Kate!" that the king was by Kate's side "to lend his cherished daughter-in-law moral support" during her health battle.
Kate's advocacy work following her cancer diagnosis continues, Nicholl told Fox News Digital.
Catherine, Princess of Wales curtseys to King Charles III on Sept. 16, 2025, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Thankfully, despite a serious health issue, she has overcome that," Nicholl said. "We've just seen her climb the three highest peaks in the United Kingdom to raise money for the Royal Marsden. She's turning her experience into something positive, and I think that's earned her a great deal of respect among the British public, along with a lot of love and affection. People are very much behind her and William."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Catherine, Princess of Wales, is seen visiting Evelina London Children's Hospital in London, on July 6, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)
Chard echoed those sentiments.

"Princess Catherine connects with people in a way that restores faith in the monarchy," Chard said. "She has learned every aspect of the institution over many years and has blended in carefully without fuss. Princess Catherine is central to the institution's success, and King Charles knows this."

With a slimmed down monarchy, Charles needs key allies now more than ever. His younger brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, stepped back as a working royal in 2019 following his controversial ties to late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Charles has since formally removed Andrew’s princely title and HRH style.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on Feb. 19, 2026, and released after about 11 hours under investigation. He was detained on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations that he shared confidential trade reports with Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the U.K.'s trade envoy. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
In 2020, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, stepped back as senior working royals and later settled in California.

From left: Prince William, Kate Middleton, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle attend a ceremony to mark the centenary of the Royal Air Force on the forecourt of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior royals in 2020. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Princess Anne and other senior working royals are all stretched thin — and none of them are young," author Catherine Mayer previously told People magazine. "William and Catherine carry the whole thing."
Sources told the outlet there had been "even greater attention and expectation on the Waleses." Still, royal experts told Fox News Digital that Kate is well-positioned to support the king.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Queen Camilla, Prince William, King Charles and Kate Middleton are seen at the "No Time To Die" world premiere at the Royal Albert Hall in London, on Sept. 28, 2021. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Naturally, King Charles recognizes the value of Kate, who is indeed the monarchy's greatest asset," Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "We should add, 'together with her partnership with William and their family.' While we praise Catherine's many strengths, William is the future king. She will one day be queen consort. They see themselves as a close-knit couple."

"William is currently at the center of reports that he and the king differ over how to handle Prince Harry, in particular," Fitzwilliams said. "As she showed when the Sussexes met with the king and Queen Camilla, she fully supports William's approach."

Catherine, Princess of Wales, speaks to guests during a Cancer Research UK reception marking the charity's 125th anniversary at St. James's Palace on June 2, 2026, in London. (Jonathan Brady - Pool/Getty Images)

As William and Kate prepare for their future roles, they are likely to remain under close public scrutiny. With Charles' support, royal experts believe the couple is well-positioned for the years ahead.
Prince William is heir to the British throne. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)

"It’s not at all surprising King Charles and Princess Catherine have bonded," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "One can tangibly feel the public also values her wonderful assets from the reception she always receives when in public, as well as in opinion polls. She has become indispensable and has won the public’s trust."

"Charles can depend on Catherine because she is consistent, steady and modern in her approach to family, shaped by her upbringing and dedication to duty," Fordwich said. "She handled the strain of her cancer battle with dignity, without any indication of self-pity."

Catherine, Princess of Wales cools down with a fan as she attends Day 14 of the 2026 Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club on July 12, 2026, in London. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
"One can observe from the body language between Charles and Catherine that they are so comfortable together, derived from the time they spent together during their cancer battles."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Jessica Simpson celebrates turning 46 in bikini and reveals her children have never seen her perform

story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Simpson reclined beneath a purple crocheted cover while wearing oval dark sunglasses. Her blonde hair was styled in a loose side braid, and she accessorized the polka-dot bikini with layered turquoise bead necklaces, a square green pendant, dangling stone earrings and stacked bracelets.

Jessica Simpson marked her 46th birthday with a bikini selfie while celebrating another trip around the sun. (Jessica Simpson/Instagram)

title: Reality TV stars clash over what really destroyed their marriage after shocking bedroom confession

story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Amanda Batula shed new light on the intimacy issues that plagued the reality TV star's marriage to Kyle Cooke, revealing the estranged couple's sex life all but disappeared years before they split.

Months after announcing their separation, Batula and Cooke opened up about their lack of intimacy at the "Summer House" reunion in June. The estranged couple later revealed more about the challenges they faced behind closed doors during the "In the City" reunion Tuesday.

Batula hinted there were issues with emotional intimacy long before the two tied the knot in 2021, revealing sex was a topic of discussion during couples' therapy ahead of their wedding. The swimsuit brand founder also attributed the lack of physical touch to her depression.
JESSIE JAMES DECKER ON WHY HER MARRIAGE TO ERIC DECKER HASN'T LOST ITS SPARK AFTER FOUR KIDS

Amanda Batula said emotional intimacy disappeared long before her split from Kyle Cooke, claiming she felt "like an object" as their marriage unraveled. The "Summer House" stars revisited their relationship struggles during the "In the City" reunion. (Jocelyn Prescod/Bravo via Getty Images)
"I wasn’t getting courted," Batula admitted, according to People. "There were no dates."

"He would work all day, work all night, then come to bed, tell me an email and then try to have sex with me," she explained. "It felt like there was no foreplay. There was no emotional intimacy. There was no conversation. There was nothing else happening in the relationship."

"I felt like I was just an object at that point," Batula added. "Then the depression hit also, and then it was just an unfortunate storm. Then he would still go out. He would still do these things. We get into big fights —"
TIM ALLEN REVEALS THE ONE THING THAT HAS SAVED HIS NEARLY 20-YEAR MARRIAGE TO JANE HAJDUK

The 85-year-old "Knots Landing" icon is taking fans by surprise with her latest career move — joining OnlyFans.

Donna Mills announced that she's joining OnlyFans this week. (Getty Images)

title: 'Lord of the Rings' star Sean Astin had to sell his home after negotiating 'small' salary for hit movie
summary: Sean Astin reveals he had to sell his house after negotiating a surprisingly small salary for the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy with no residuals.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Sean Astin captured the hearts of fantasy fans everywhere when he starred as Samwise Gamgee in the "Lord of the Rings" but says the compensation was not what one would expect.
In a new interview with The Guardian, the 55-year-old actor shared just how "small" his payday was for the successful Academy Award-winning trilogy.

"I was not prepared for that level of visibility and access," he said. "And there was a disconnect between the attention that I was getting and how much money we had. It was not a lot of money. In fact, I had to sell my house because I negotiated such a small amount on the trilogy."
He revealed in a November 2017 interview on the "Jim and Sam Show" that he made $250,000 for his work on the trilogy in addition to some profit from merchandise sales, but no residuals.
Astin shared that his paycheck for "Lord of the Rings" was not as big as everyone probably thinks. (New Line/courtesy Everett Collection; Frazer Harrison/WireImage)
'MARRIED... WITH CHILDREN' STAR TED MCGINLEY REVEALS HE GETS PENNY RESIDUAL CHECKS FROM HIS HIT TV SHOWS
The "Stranger Things" star said he had purchased a home in Los Angeles and was told he needed to make $250,000 a year to pay the mortgage when he got the role in the films.

"It was an offer for $250,000 for a year and a half," he said. "And I was like, ‘Wait a minute, my pen signed this contract, which obligated me to $250,000 a year, and I’m gonna sign this contract, which will make it so that I absolutely cannot satisfy that other thing.'"
He added that, in the end, it was all about negotiating. He also clarified that by the time the third movie was released, he "was feeling a little bit better" in terms of finances.
"By then, I had done a lot of other work, and we were fine," he added.

Astin's co-star in the first installment of the trilogy, Cate Blanchett, who played Galadriel, also spoke about how little she was paid for her role, telling Andy Cohen in an August 2024 episode of "Watch What Happens Live," "No one got paid anything to do that movie."
Astin said he was paid $250,000 for all three films combined. (JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I wanted to work with the guy who made 'Braindead,'" she said about why she took the role despite the low pay. "I mean, I basically got free sandwiches. And I got to keep my ears, which is something."

Other cast members, including Orlando Bloom and Elijah Wood, have also spoken about how little they were paid for their work in the films, with Bloom telling Howard Stern in 2019 he was paid $175,000 for the trilogy.
Also starring Viggo Mortensen, Sean Bean and Ian McKellen, the trilogy became a huge blockbuster success.
The first film, "Fellowship of the Ring," raked in about $897 million at the worldwide box office, with its sequels bringing in about $945 million and $1.15 billion, respectively.

The films also starred Sean Bean, Ian McKellan, Elijah Wood, Orlando Bloom and others. (Frank Micelotta/ImageDirect)

All three films were also critically acclaimed, earning a combined 30 Academy Award nominations and 17 wins. The third film alone, "Return of the King," won all 11 categories it was nominated in, including best picture, tying the record for the most Oscars won by a single film.

title: Tim Robbins turns to ayahuasca after feeling 'consumed by anger' over cancel culture
summary: Tim Robbins tells Joe Rogan how an ayahuasca ceremony helped him release years of frustration over cancel culture and political polarization.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Oscar-winning actor Tim Robbins says an ayahuasca trip helped him break free from the anger he felt over America's deep divide.
Robbins revealed the psychedelic experience left him feeling "completely lighter" after years of frustration with cancel culture and political polarization.
The "Shawshank Redemption" star said he turned to the Amazonian psychedelic brew with one goal in mind — to stop being "consumed" by outrage over what he sees as the unraveling of modern society.
KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS
Tim Robbins told Joe Rogan how an ayahuasca ceremony helped him release years of frustration over cancel culture and political polarization. (Ernesto Ruscio / Getty Images)

"They tell you to go in with an intention," Robbins said during a candid appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience." "My intention was to … I was frustrated with feeling anger about what was going on in the world, and I said, 'I want to release that. I don't want to be consumed by that anger.'"
Robbins said his psychedelic experience was an intense spiritual journey that included what he described as an encounter with his late mother.
"What she said was, 'You're injured. You're a warrior, and you're injured and you need to rest, but the fight's not over,'" Robbins recalled.
When Joe Rogan asked what battle he believed he was fighting, Robbins pointed squarely at today's culture wars.
Robbins described his intense psychedelic journey that included an encounter with his late mother and left him feeling "completely lighter." (Tristan Fewings / Getty Images)

"I was battling my frustration with the dissolution of society, people being angry at each other over ridiculous things, long friendships being affected, people being canceled for expressing their opinion, all this stuff," he said. "And I wanted out. I wanted to be absolved of that. I didn't want to be engaged in it."
Although Robbins acknowledged skeptics would dismiss the experience, he said it profoundly changed him.
"I definitely felt her presence there. It was no doubt it was her," he said, adding that by the end of the ceremony he felt "completely lighter" and reconnected with his late mother.

The Oscar-winning actor also compared cancel culture to Soviet Union tactics after Eastern Europe audience members drew parallels to communism. (Presley Ann/Getty Images for TCM)
Earlier in the conversation, Robbins also spoke about the hot-button issue, arguing that cancel culture bears striking similarities to tactics used under the former Soviet Union.
The actor recalled touring Eastern Europe with his play "Topsy Turvy," where he asked audience members in Romania what aspects of modern life reminded them of the communist era.
"They said, 'Without a doubt, cancel culture,'" Robbins recounted.

According to Robbins, audience members described how Soviet authorities allegedly kept damaging personal files on citizens and weaponized them against anyone who stepped out of line.
Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins starred together in "The Shawshank Redemption." (Paul Archuleta/FilmMagic)

"'Well, Soviet Union used to keep files on all of us, right?'" he recalled the person saying. "'So, as long as you're a good party member, there wouldn't be a thing said. But once you stepped out of line, they brought out that old file. Now that affair with your secretary from 30 years ago is going to ruin your life. They're going to ruin your family. They're going to kill your career. And they're going to make a big public display of it to show other people to stay in line.'"

"They felt like cancel culture was basically operating in the same way as the Soviet Union did," Robbins said. "It was really interesting to see that perspective in Eastern Europe — people that have, you know, lived under that kind of oppressive situation and their perspective on modern day."

title: Tom Selleck says 'Blue Bloods' cast made major sacrifice to save show before cancellation
summary: Tom Selleck reveals the "Blue Bloods" cast took a 25% salary cut to keep the show going, yet the series still ended despite ranking sixth in ratings.
story: Donnie Wahlberg and Jenny McCarthy told Fox News Digital that they prefer ordering takeout and watching the faith-based TV show for date nights.
Tom Selleck addressed the "very frustrating" end to "Blue Bloods," saying the cast had already taken a 25% salary cut to keep it on the air despite it still ranking in sixth place in broadcast shows.
"They claim 14, but it was 15. We did 15 seasons, 293 episodes," Selleck told Ted Danson on his "Where Everybody Knows Your Name" podcast Wednesday. "’Blue Bloods’ was a labor of love for everybody.

"Maybe people don't realize, but a lot of shows become miserable to work on. You get a lot of egos, and ‘I'm not coming out of my dressing room ‘til he's coming out,’ and it's miserable. It's absolutely miserable."
TED DANSON WAS SHOCKED WOMEN VIEWED HIM AS A SEX SYMBOL DURING EARLY ‘CHEERS’ DAYS
Tom Selleck poses with "Blue Bloods" castmates Bridget Moynahan and Donnie Wahlberg in 2014. (GC Images)
But he said "Blue Bloods" was never like that.
Knowing that his character was the patriarch of the family on the show, he decided to "set an example."

"Either way, everybody got it," he continued, saying that, in the last year of the show, "at our last family dinner, everybody wanted to come back. We'd already taken a 25% cut in salary. We'd already done all sorts of things to keep the show going. But the show was, it was very frustrating 'cause ‘Blue Bloods’ was out of the top 100 shows on broadcast television, ‘Blue Bloods’ was No. 6 in our 15th year."
ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION
The 81-year-old actor reiterated that "nobody wanted to leave. Everybody was gonna stay on. That's hard to get. It may be some kind of record to have the same cast intact for that length of time."
The cast might have made different decisions if it wasn’t a family, "but, you know, you couldn't very well replace Jamie [Will Estes] or Danny [Donnie Wahlberg] or anybody with another actor."
